sections.h2: Provident funds pay 7.1% and 8.25%, fixed by government rather than markets

chart.title: PPF has held at 7.1% since April 2020, and EPF at 8.25% for FY2025-26
chart.source: Ministry of Finance; EPFO Central Board of Trustees.

sections.means: Both rates are safe because the government sets them, but PPF locks money for 15 years and EPF is meant for retirement or defined life events.
sections.todo: Treat PPF and EPF as the capital-protection floor of the plate, not as the growth engine.

sections.h2: Indian equity indices have returned 11.8% to 15.4% a year over long windows

chart.title: Index returns beat the 8.25% EPF rate over long windows, though they are not guaranteed
chart.source: Market-data aggregation of NSE and BSE indices, as of February 2026.

sections.means: Equity indices delivered higher long-run returns than either provident fund, but with year-to-year volatility that the administered rates do not carry.
sections.todo: Use a mutual fund or SIP for the growth share of the plate, knowing a single year can fall well below these averages.

sections.h2: Gold's ten-year return rose into a 13.5% to 16.5% band for windows to mid-2026

chart.title: Gold's ten-year return moved up from about 10-11% after the 2025-26 rally
chart.sub: Gold CAGR in India, % p.a., approximate bands from market-data sources.
chart.source: Secondary market-data sources; not a single official series.

sections.means: Gold moves differently from Indian equities and has tended to hold up when stock markets fell, though this is not guaranteed in every downturn.
sections.todo: Hold gold as a hedge alongside equity, and use physical gold, gold ETFs, gold funds or digital gold now that new Sovereign Gold Bond issues have stopped.

sections.h2: The latest SEBI warning on unlisted-share platforms followed earlier ones in 2016 and 2024

chart.title: Each SEBI warning targets unauthorised platforms, and the June 2026 advisory names the risks
events: First advisory against unauthorised unlisted-securities platforms
Second advisory on the same subject
Third advisory, PR 32/2026: no grievance redress, forged-certificate risk

sections.means: The June 2026 advisory names specific risks: no exchange-level grievance redress, misleading listing-gain marketing and counterparty risk including forged share certificates.
sections.todo: Buy unlisted shares only through regulated intermediaries or employee stock schemes, and never through an unauthorised platform.
